initialize()

The initialize() method activates a FeatureCell within the Vault runtime and begins its initialization cycle. Initialization binds declared behaviors, controllers, and fluent configuration into a deterministic execution pipeline.

Method Contract Summary

  • Initialization is required before any FeatureCell interaction
  • Initialization activates the FeatureCell runtime pipeline
  • Initialization occurs exactly once per FeatureCell
  • Initialization may enqueue an initial replaceState operation
  • Errors during initialization prevent FeatureCell operation

The initialize() method defines activation and readiness. It does not directly mutate state. Instead, it evaluates the configured initialization mechanism and, if applicable, enqueues a deterministic replaceState operation through the pipeline.

Note

initialize() must be called before a FeatureCell can be used. Any attempt to read state, issue updates, or interact with a FeatureCell before initialization results in a runtime error. A FeatureCell that is not initialized is non-operational.

What initialize() Does

Calling initialize() transitions the FeatureCell from a configured definition into an active runtime participant.

  • Validates FeatureCell configuration and declared behaviors
  • Registers the FeatureCell with the Vault runtime
  • Activates the Conductor execution surface
  • Evaluates the declared initialization source (if any)
  • Enqueues the initial state candidate through the pipeline (if applicable)

Initialization does not bypass the pipeline. Any initial value produced by hydrate(), Persist behaviors, or descriptor.initialState is processed as a standard replaceState operation.

If no initialization mechanism is declared, the FeatureCell becomes active with value: undefined and awaits explicit replaceState() calls.

Initialization Flow

During initialization, Vault evaluates exactly one initialization source according to precedence rules:

  1. hydrate() (highest precedence)
  2. Persist behaviors
  3. descriptor.initialState
  4. No source declared (manual initialization required)

Only one source is evaluated. Initialization sources are not fallback layers. If the selected source throws, initialization fails. If it resolves to undefined, no write occurs.

Any produced value is passed through the full pipeline — Resolve, Operators, Filters, Reducers, and Emit — exactly as if replaceState() had been called manually.

Diagrams
Pipeline Initialization Flow
Initialization Rules
  • Initialization may be called exactly once
  • Calling initialize() more than once results in a runtime error
  • Initialization must complete successfully for the FeatureCell to remain usable
  • Vault must be initialized before FeatureCells are initialized

If initialization fails due to a thrown error in the selected initialization source, the FeatureCell does not activate partially and no fallback source is evaluated.

Method Contract
Runtime Invocation
Method Description
initialize()

inputs:

  • none

returns:

  • void
 Activates the FeatureCell runtime and executes the initialization cycle. If an initialization source is declared, its value is processed as a deterministic replaceState operation.
Example

Example: Basic Initialization

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {  
        key: 'employees',
        // Initial state is declared directly in the descriptor
        initialState: [
          { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
          { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
        ]
      }
    )
  ]
};

@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    // Initial state is declared directly in the descriptor
    initialState: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
    ]
  },
);

employeeCell.initialize();

`}}

Example: hydrate() + initialize()

{{`@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault
      .hydrate(() => Promise.resolve(...))
      .initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    // ignored
    initialState: []
  }
);

employeeCell.hydrate(() => Promise.resolve(...)).initialize();

`}}
Lifecycle Notes

All fluent configuration methods (filters, reducers, taps, errors, emitStates, and others) must be declared before calling initialize().

Initialization establishes the execution boundary of a FeatureCell. Pipelines execute only after initialization has completed.

Initialization does not guarantee that a produced value commits to state. Because the initial candidate passes through the full pipeline, it may be transformed or filtered according to installed logic.
